name: Curse of Misfortune
body:
One bad day is all it takes.

Bonus Spells: 0th—chance*, 1st—compel hostility, 2nd—locate weakness, 3rd—screech, 4th—pessimism

Curse Manifestation

Some lathspells bear a curse that pulls at fate and bends it only towards its worst conclusions. This manifests an aura where chance is weighted against all within it. Whenever a creature within 10 feet of the lathspell (including themselves) would be subject to an effect with a rolled duration add one to the result. In addition these creatures also reduce any mischance from concealment they benefit from by 10%.

Curse Abilities
Adjustable Outcome (Su)

Misfortune for their enemies means the lathspell often still lands glancing blows in combat. Whenever you make a weapon attack against an enemy within 30 feet and the attack misses by 2 or less you still deal minimum damage to the target of your attack. This triggers even if the attack roll was a natural 1, so long as the calculated result of the attack misses by 2 or less. The description of how the damage is still dealt should include the otherwise spectacular failure.

Balancing the Scales (Su)

Prerequisite(s) 6th level or higher

Misfortune befalls a lathspell’s enemies when they believe they have the upper hand. Whenever you would be subject to precision damage you may make a special attack against the source of the damage as an immediate action. If the source of the precision damage was a melee attack, you may make an attack of opportunity against your attacker. If the attack hits, you add the same amount of precision damage to your attack as was dealt to you. This attack of opportunity can be made even if you are flat footed, though not if you are unconscious or otherwise unable to perceive the attacker. If the precision damage was caused by a ranged attack within 30 feet, the attacking creature must make a Will save using your lathspell curse DC or take damage equal to the amount of precision damage dealt to you.

Curse of Unluck (Su)

Prerequisite(s) 6th level or higher

The lathspell delights in imposing misfortune on others. As a standard action you can impart this misfortune onto a target as a touch attack. The target must make a Will saving throw using the lathspell’s curse DC or become stricken with debilitatingly bad luck. On a failure, for 24 hours, the target must roll all attack rolls, ability checks, skill checks, and saving throws twice and take the worse result. On a success the creature becomes nauseated until the beginning of your next turn. In either case the curse of misfortune is fickle and a creature can only be targeted once per day whether they succeed or fail. This curse can be removed by a break enchantment using your class level as the caster level of the curse. A casting of remove curse can suppress the effect of this curse for 1 hour.

Erratic Fortune (Su)

For every bit of bad luck there is a little bit of good as well. Whenever you are dealt damage by a weapon attack you gain a +1 luck bonus to AC until the end of the attacker’s next turn; this bonus improves by +1 for every four class levels you have attained. When this bonus ends, you gain a -1 penalty to attack rolls until the end of your next turn.

Fateful Openings (Su)

Misfortune is a fickle curse, but easy enough to turn to the lathspell’s advantage. You can project an aura as a move action that makes combat more deadly, with each creature within 10 feet of the you receiving a penalty to their AC against critical confirmation rolls equal to your Charisma modifier.

Loaded Dice (Su)

The lathspell with this curse is always living recklessly at the whims of fate. You may single out a foe within 60 feet as a standard action. The target makes a Will save at the your lathspell curse DC or your fates become intertwined. Whenever you or your target would roll damage against each other you roll all damage twice and use the higher total. This effect applies only to any hit point damage that would be dealt to either creature but not to any ability damage, ability drain, or any other effect which deals damage to an attribute other than hit points. This effect lasts until either you or your target are knocked unconscious or killed, or combat ends.

You can maintain only a single instance of loaded dice at any given time.

Mirrored Fate (Su)

Misfortune that befalls the lathspell can often befall their foes as well.

Whenever the lathspell fails a saving throw to a non-damaging spell or effect they may make a caster level check against a DC of 11 + the caster level of the spell they were affected by. If they succeed, the caster of the spell is also affected at the same save DC. Using this ability is an immediate action and the lathspell takes an amount of untyped damage equal to twice the level of the affected spell when they succeed at the caster level check as the magical energies surge through them and return to their caster.

Shadow Raven (Su)

The curse of misfortune provides a shadowy companion representing bad luck; the shadow raven. The shadow raven is treated as a raven familiar, using your lathspell class level in place of your wizard level. Unlike a normal raven, it grants you a +3 bonus on Stealth checks rather than on Appraise checks. At 7th level, any creature adjacent to the shadow raven other than yourself is treated as being within your cloak of menace ability. At 12th level, the shadow raven can deliver the effects of other curse abilities granted by the curse of misfortune in place of its master; two instances of the same curse ability do not stack and the shadow raven uses the same save DC as you for these effects, if applicable.

Tipping the Scales (Su)

Prerequisite(s) 10th level or higher

Through many trials and experiences with their curse, the lathspell learns to focus it to also aid the luck of their friends and allies. As a full round action, you can imbue all allies within 30 feet with a bit of the luck stolen by the curse of misfortune for a number of rounds equal to your Charisma modifier. Once per round, the affected creatures may roll each of one attack roll, one saving throw, and one skill check twice and take the better result.

The lathspell may use this ability a number of times per day equal to their Constitution modifier, as it takes a great toll on their stamina.

Vicious Luck (Su)

Prerequisite(s) 6th level or higher

The curse of misfortune has a tendency to punish the unlucky more severely than they would be otherwise. Whenever an enemy within 10 feet of you fails a saving throw or attack roll by 5 or more they suffer further harm than anticipated and are dealt damage equal to your class level. This damage is untyped and bypasses all damage reduction and energy resistances or immunities.

Walking Curse
The Hand on the Scales (Su)

The scion of misfortune walks unseen and changes events at whim, bending them towards their own ends. The lathspell gains immunity to divination effects (unless they wish to be affected by them), and gains a pool of fortune equal to their Charisma modifier which replenishes after 8 hours of rest. The fortune may be spent to apply a bonus or penalty to an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw made within 30 feet of the lathspell as a free action. The bonus or penalty is equal to the lathspell’s Charisma modifier.
